methodological_rigor.justification: The study employs LASSO-Cox regression with appropriate variable prespecification, 500-bootstrap internal validation, calibration plots, DCA, and time-dependent AUC—a methodologically sound nomogram development framework. The cohort is well-characterized with standardized treatment protocols from two consecutive prospective trials, and missing data are handled by random forest imputation. Key limitations include the small event count (22 deaths, 28 relapses), which risks overfitting despite LASSO shrinkage; single-center design limiting generalizability; and the use of two temporally distinct regimens as a covariate without controlling for calendar-time confounding in supportive care. HSCT is analyzed without time-dependent modeling, introducing potential immortal time bias.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: RUNX1::RUNX1T1-positive AML represents the most common cytogenetic AML subtype in children, and improving relapse prediction directly informs post-remission decisions (HSCT, MRD-adapted therapy). The nomograms integrate High-Risk MRD, WBC, treatment regimen, BM blasts by FCM, and EMI—all clinically available variables—making this practically deployable tool highly relevant for risk-adapted management. The 3-year endpoint is clinically meaningful, and superior predictive performance over individual biomarkers supports clinical utility. External validation in a multicenter setting is the critical next step before adoption.

reporting_quality.justification: The manuscript adheres to most REMARK criteria for prognostic marker reporting: prespecified candidate variables with biological rationale, complete LASSO/Cox model reporting with HRs and CIs, Kaplan-Meier risk stratification, and model discrimination/calibration statistics. Decision curve analysis and bootstrap validation are reported per best practice guidelines. Gaps include absence of a TRIPOD table (applicable to prediction model development), no public data or code deposition, and some confidence intervals for rare subgroups are wide and potentially unstable. Flow diagram and patient exclusion criteria are clearly documented.

novelty_literature.justification: This is the first nomogram-based prediction model specifically developed for pediatric RUNX1::RUNX1T1-positive AML achieving CR after a single induction course in a Chinese cohort, filling a meaningful gap. Prior work from this group (reference 14) established the High-Risk MRD criterion; this paper integrates it with additional clinical variables into a deployable risk tool. The novelty is methodological (nomogram construction with comprehensive validation) rather than mechanistic, and comparable nomograms exist for adult AML and other pediatric AML subtypes.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly written with well-organized sections and logical flow from methods through results to clinical implications. Statistical reporting is thorough—C-indices, AUCs with time-point specificity, and calibration curves are all referenced. The discussion appropriately contextualizes findings with prior literature and honestly addresses study limitations including the small event count and single-center design. A minor issue is that the DCA figure is relegated to a supplementary figure without detailed narrative description in the methods.

key_strengths: LASSO-Cox framework with REMARK-compliant reporting, calibration plots, DCA, and 500-bootstrap internal validation
Clinical variables are all routinely available at diagnosis and early treatment assessment, enhancing practical deployability
First nomogram for pediatric RUNX1::RUNX1T1-positive AML integrating dynamic MRD kinetics with baseline clinical features
key_concerns: Small event count (22 deaths, 28 relapses) relative to the number of candidate predictors risks overfitting despite LASSO regularization
No external validation cohort; bootstrap internal validation alone is insufficient to support clinical adoption
Temporal confounding from two sequential regimens (2009 vs 2016) cannot be fully adjusted by statistical methods alone
HSCT modeled without time-dependent covariate, introducing potential immortal time bias
chief_reviewer.rationale: Methodologically sound nomogram study limited primarily by small event count and single-center design; appropriate for tier 3 with minor revisions addressing HSCT modeling and clearer reporting of DCA results.
